nodes.title: Positive diagonal potential comparison
nodes.statement: On D², μ=χ/(1+√(1−χ))² is smooth, including Δ, and F=−8πlog(1−μ) is smooth psh. Extend log μ by −∞ on Δ; it is psh and locally integrable. checked.note: BT fixes curvature −1; the pinned disc distance is artanh of the quotient modulus, so the factor two is required. No new metric instance is planned.
The pinned norm_discCoordinate formula is tanh(dist/2); combine it with the pinned disc distance at zero and artanh_tanh. BT supplies the normalization, not this Lean comparison.
BT’s centered disc has Euclidean radius tanh(r/2). Nonpositive radii give the empty set; the local signatures and three examples preserve that boundary.
Converting BT’s 2i dz∧d z̄ form into dx∧dy gives 4/(1−|z|²)². Tests distinguish the factor four, conjugation and boundary blowup.
The restricted weighted Lebesgue construction matches the form. Added the half-disc value 4π/3 because every old test also admitted the zero measure.
BT’s a(r)=4πsinh²(r/2) applies geometrically for r≥0. The total scalar formula and tests make no negative-radius area claim.
Polar integration of the density gives 4πt²/(1−t²), t=tanh(r/2), including zero radius. The pinned nonnegative polar theorem needs no integrability hypothesis.
BT Remark 24 permits constant tensor scaling. In dimension two area gains λ², distance gains λ, and the radius argument becomes r/λ; scalar signatures do not assert an unbuilt curvature theorem.
BT uses coordinatewise maximum neighborhoods with the sum area form. Empty Fin 0 products and nonpositive radii are treated separately; no sum-distance substitution occurs.
BT Lemma 13/Figure 2 gives M(R)=2artanh√tanh(R/2), with cosh M=e^R. Positivity, monotonicity and this identity detect radius normalization errors.
BT’s isometry-normalized intersection of the two balls gives the stated enclosure for 0≤a<1 and R>0, including a=0. The quotient version later retains simultaneous lifts.
BT uses tanh²(d₁/4). Because hyperbolicDist=d₁/2 at the pin, the local scalar definition uses tanh²(hyperbolicDist/2).
BT’s quotient modulus squared equals tanh²(d₁/2). The local total formula has geometric meaning only with both arguments in the disc.
The hyperbolic double-angle identity gives χ=4μ/(1+μ)² and 1−χ=(1−μ)²/(1+μ)². All denominators are positive on the disc.
The erratum replaces the second coordinate by its conjugate; expansion gives |z−w̄|²/|1−zw|² and the real conjugate graph as zero set.
The erratum treats the conjugate graph as totally real. The vectors (1,1) and (i,i) explicitly separate its tangent plane from a complex line.
BT sets F=−8πlog(1−μ). It is finite across μ=0; its nonnegativity is local scalar algebra, while positivity and domination are separate HV.3 claims.
BT Proposition 23 expands log(χ/(1−χ)) as H(log μ). The s<0 domain and derivative cosh r are correct; the pole value is handled by currents, not Real.log at zero.
The erratum uses −log(1−ψ)=2log cosh(d/2). The scalar domain is 0≤ψ<1; the current identity is separately specified.
The erratum uses g(t)=2asin√(1−e^(−t)) with derivative 1/√(e^t−1). Its derivative decreases; positivity of the composite cannot be inferred from convex composition.
Pull back BT’s sum form along holomorphic coordinates: each density contributes b(f_i)|f_i′|². Constant coordinates vanish; the derivative chain rule gives reparameterization compatibility.
Integrating the nonnegative pulled-back density counts source multiplicity. Added the positive half-disc fibre test because the old zero/constant/additivity tests admitted identically zero volume.
Direct integration of the local fibre density gives a(r). BT’s Theorem 19 equality model is the one-coordinate fibre, independent of the fixed disc coordinate.
On t↦(t,−t) both densities agree, μ=|t|² and the diagonal order is one; BT’s equality example therefore has volume 2a(r).
This is a derived polar integral, not a separately named BT theorem. The derivative d t^(d−1) yields d times the image-disc area; injective change of variables alone would lose that factor.
